title: dograh-hq/dograh — Open source voice AI platform. Self-hosted alternative to Vapi and Retell. On Prem, BYOK across Speech to Speech or LLM/STT/TTS, with a visual workflow builder, MCP native and telephony support.
content:
The open-source, self-hostable alternative to Vapi & Retell — build production voice agents with a visual workflow builder, test them in minutes, and let AI coding assistants help design and edit them through MCP.
📖 Docs · 📜 BSD 2-Clause · 🌐 中文 · 🌐 日本語
- 100% open source, self-hostable — no vendor lock-in, unlike Vapi or Retell
- Full control & transparency — every line of code is open, with flexible LLM / TTS / STT integration
- Maintained by YC alumni and exit founders, committed to keeping voice AI open
An honest comparison on the axes that matter most to teams evaluating voice AI platforms.
Note
We collect anonymous usage data to improve the product. You can opt out by setting ENABLE_TELEMETRY=false before running the startup script.
Note If you wish to run the platform on a remote server instead, checkout our Documentation
curl -o docker-compose.yaml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dograh-hq/dograh/main/docker-compose.yaml && curl -o start_docker.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dograh-hq/dograh/main/scripts/start_docker.sh && chmod +x start_docker.sh && ./start_docker.sh
Note
By default the quickstart starts a public *.trycloudflare.com quick tunnel to the API (for inbound telephony webhooks), and signup is enabled. After creating your first account, you can close signup by setting ENABLE_SIGNUP=false in .env and re-running ./start_docker.sh (docker compose restart does not apply .env changes).
⚡ Prefer an AI agent to set it up for you? If you use Claude Code or Codex, install the official Dograh setup skill and let your agent handle installation, configuration, and troubleshooting — it detects your OS, picks the right deploy path, runs Dograh's own setup scripts, and verifies the result.
# In Claude Code
/plugin marketplace add dograh-hq/dograh-plugins
/plugin install dograh@dograh
Then start a new session and ask it to "set up Dograh" (or run /dograh-setup). Codex is supported too — see the plugin repo.
Note First startup may take 2-3 minutes to download all images. Once running, open http://localhost:3010 to create your first AI voice assistant! For common issues and solutions, see 🔧 Troubleshooting.
- Open http://localhost:3010 in your browser.
- Pick Inbound or Outbound, name your bot (e.g. Lead Qualification), and describe the use case in 5–10 words (e.g. Screen insurance form submissions for purchase intent).
- Click Test Agent.
- Use Test Audio to talk to your agent in the browser, or Test Chat to iterate faster in text. In Test Chat, you can edit or replay user turns and Dograh will regenerate the agent's replies and node transitions from that point.
🔑 No API keys needed. Dograh ships with auto-generated keys and its own LLM / TTS / STT stack. Connect your own keys for LLM, TTS, STT, or Telephony (e.g. Twilio, Vonage, Telnyx) anytime.
Featured On & Community Validation: Dograh was named #1 Product of the Day on Product Hunt.
Dograh ships with an MCP server, so coding agents can work directly inside your Dograh workspace.
Connect Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client to inspect existing agents, search Dograh docs, fetch node schemas, create new workflows, and save draft edits from natural language.
When asking your coding agent to build a voice agent, share a short script for the use case instead of only a one-line prompt. Include the agent persona, call flow, rules, objection handling, success criteria, and a sample conversation if you have one.
See the MCP guide to connect your assistant.
- Visual workflow builder with start nodes, agent nodes, global instructions, tools, transitions, and end-call outcomes
- Test Agent panel with Test Audio for browser voice testing and Test Chat for fast prompt iteration
- QA node, knowledge bases, webhooks, embeds, and tool calling for production workflows
- Built-in telephony integrations including Twilio, Vonage, Telnyx, Plivo, Vobiz, Cloudonix, and Asterisk ARI
- Human handoff with call transfer on supported telephony providers
- Bring your own LLM, TTS, STT, and telephony providers; store artifacts in bundled MinIO or AWS/S3-compatible storage
- One-command Docker setup for self-hosting
- Python backend and modular provider architecture for customization
- Python and Node SDKs for programmatic agent creation and outbound calls
Refer Local Setup
For detailed deployment instructions including remote server setup with HTTPS, see our Docker Deployment Guide.
Visit https://www.dograh.com for our managed cloud offering.
You can go to https://docs.dograh.com for our documentation.
- Python SDK — pypi.org/project/dograh-sdk
- Node SDK — npmjs.com/package/@dograh/sdk
👋 Coming from the Better Stack video? Drop your use case in our pinned GitHub Discussion — we read every reply and the founders personally onboard early adopters.

- GitHub Discussions — share use cases, ask questions, swap workflow recipes.
- GitHub Issues — report bugs or request features.

report.summary: Dograh releases an open-source, self-hostable voice AI platform pitched as a free alternative to Vapi and Retell, with a visual workflow builder, MCP support and bring-your-own model providers.
report.background: Voice agents moved from demo to production over the past two years, and closed SaaS platforms such as Vapi and Retell came to dominate the orchestration layer — the part that stitches together speech recognition, an LLM, text-to-speech and telephony into a working call flow. That convenience came with trade-offs teams increasingly resent: per-minute platform fees, opaque pricing, data leaving their infrastructure, and little ability to swap models or tweak internals. Meanwhile the open-source building blocks matured — LiveKit, Pipecat and Vocode made low-latency audio pipelines accessible, and providers like Twilio, Telnyx and Vonage exposed clean telephony APIs. What was missing was a packaged, production-grade platform rather than a bare framework. Dograh targets exactly that gap, offering the full product experience — workflow builder, testing, telephony, SDKs — under a permissive BSD 2-Clause licence, backed by YC alumni and exit founders.
key_points: Dograh is 100% open source under BSD 2-Clause and installs with a single Docker command, so teams can run it entirely on their own infrastructure. Unlike Vapi or Retell there is no vendor lock-in and no per-minute platform fee. Anonymous telemetry is on by default but can be disabled with an environment variable, and signup can be closed after the first account is created.

It is genuinely bring-your-own-stack: you can run a speech-to-speech model end to end, or mix and match separate LLM, STT and TTS providers. Telephony integrations cover Twilio, Vonage, Telnyx, Plivo, Vobiz, Cloudonix and Asterisk ARI, and call artifacts can be stored in bundled MinIO or any S3-compatible bucket. Built-in keys work out of the box for testing.

The visual workflow builder uses start nodes, agent nodes, global instructions, tools, transitions and end-call outcomes. A Test Agent panel offers browser-based voice testing plus a Test Chat mode where you can edit or replay user turns and have Dograh regenerate the agent's replies and node transitions from that point — fast prompt iteration without burning phone calls.

MCP is native. Dograh ships an MCP server so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any MCP client can inspect existing agents, search documentation, fetch node schemas, create workflows and save draft edits from natural language. There is even a Claude Code plugin that handles installation, configuration and troubleshooting automatically.

Production features go beyond prototyping: a QA node, knowledge bases, webhooks, embeddable widgets, tool calling, human handoff with call transfer on supported carriers, a modular Python backend, and both Python and Node SDKs for programmatic agent creation and outbound dialling. The project was named #1 Product of the Day on Product Hunt.
report.impact: For the AI industry this is another step in commoditising the orchestration layer of voice agents. When a credible, BSD-licensed platform offers what Vapi and Retell charge for, the defensible value shifts to model quality, latency, telephony reliability and support — and hosted vendors face pressure to justify their margins or move upmarket. For developers, Dograh is useful twice over: as a deployable product and as a readable reference architecture showing how a real voice pipeline is wired. The trade-off is operational — you now own uptime, scaling, security and compliance, and a young project's longevity is always a question. For end users, self-hosting promises cheaper calls and better data privacy, though call quality will increasingly depend on how well each deployment is tuned. Watch whether the community sustains momentum beyond the launch.
report.tools: Start with the Dograh repo and docs.dograh.com, and try the docker-compose quickstart locally before committing. Adjacent projects worth studying are Pipecat and LiveKit Agents for audio pipelines, Vocode for simpler prototypes, and MinIO for artifact storage. On the telephony side, Twilio and Telnyx both offer free trial credit. Pair Dograh with an MCP client such as Claude Code or Cursor for agent-assisted workflow building, and consider Langfuse or similar for observability once you move past testing.
